messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: SEV2 — Private VPC egress failures for customer RadiantMed (tenant radial-523). Symptoms: intermittent 502s and TLS timeouts to hosted model endpoints from their subnets. Affected dedicated pool: radpool-3. Please acknowledge and start mitigation.

sre_jake: acked. I'm oncall. starting triage. any recent infra changes to radpool-3 networking? :mag:

net_zoe: Not from net infra side in last 24h. I see a config push to the shared egress SG last hour that touched ephemeral range rules — looking now.

alice_se: Customer reports spike ~ 08:12 UTC and degraded inference latency. They see many requests fail with "upstream reset" and some TLS handshake timeouts. I have a repro curl from their private subnet: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
* Connected to api.redwood.example (52.27.10.142) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Operation timed out after 300000 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

eng_sam: Can you share NLB target health for radpool-3? pinging control plane for status.

ops-bot: Control-plane event: upstream-rule-change applied to security-group sg-0a1b2c3d at 08:09 UTC by deploy-bot (change-id: cfg-20260317-0912).

net_zoe: Found it — deploy-bot removed a broad egress allow for 32768-61000 and replaced with stricter set for internal services only. That broke a customer-hosted sidecar/proxy that uses ephemeral ports to maintain TLS to model endpoints. Targets to NLB are fine (healthy), but connections from tenant subnets are being rejected at the SG.

sre_jake: Confirming — I see SYNs from 10.52.33.0/24 reaching NLB but the backend is sending RSTs. Conntrack logs on radial-523 NAT instances show TCP RST after stage 2. Likely SG drop on return-path.

alice_se: Customer_oncall on the line — @customer_oncall can you validate if you rolled anything at 08:09 UTC?

customer_oncall: We didn't. Our sidecar hasn't changed. We see success for a few minutes then mass failures. It's impacting live inference for two production services. Estimated P50 latency doubled and p95 errors ~ 35%.

pm_ravi: Impact: 1 enterprise customer (RadiantMed) on Dedicated — high business impact. Let's push a quick mitigation and then follow with root cause. Options: revert deploy-bot SG change, or add a targeted rule for radial-523 ephemeral range to the egress SG for radpool-3. Preference for minimal blast radius.

net_zoe: I can add a specific rule: allow outbound from 10.52.33.0/24 to 52.27.10.142/32 port 443 and ephemeral return ports 32768-61000 for the next 30 mins. Applying now.

sre_jake: Applying temporary SG rule. Runbook command: 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.52.33.0/24 --description "temp allow radiomed egress to model endpoints"
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 32768-61000 --cidr 10.52.33.0/24 --description "temp ephemeral allow"
```

ops-bot: Change queued and executed by sre_jake at 08:18 UTC (change-id: hotfix-20260317-0818).

alice_se: We got initial confirmation from RadiantMed — requests started succeeding ~08:20 UTC and error rate dropped. Customer reports degraded but functioning. They want a postmortem and a permanent fix plan.

eng_sam: Next steps: 1) Reproduce in staging with the stricter SG to validate failure mode. 2) Update deploy-bot change template to include tenant ephemeral exceptions when deploying to shared egress SG OR move tenant pool to dedicated SG that doesn't inherit the restrictive rule. 3) Runbook update: require e2e test for private VPC egress after infra changes.

sre_jake: I'll keep the temp rule for 1 hour, monitor metrics and then coordinate rollback once devs confirm safe permanence path. Paging followups: paging list updated, assign to net_zoe + eng_sam for RCA.

pm_ravi: I'll inform account team and schedule postmortem with RadiantMed. Thanks all — nice fast triage. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident state -> mitigated (manual SG exception applied). Severity stays SEV2 until RCA complete.
